nodes.label: Microsoft
nodes.relation: Buys NVIDIA racks for Azure and runs Vera Rubin NVL72 systems
nodes.summary: Azure grew 48% last quarter and Microsoft says it still cannot build capacity fast enough to meet demand.
brief: Its capex is one of the four budgets that set NVIDIA's data center demand.
nodes.health: Azure grew 48% and capex is guided above $50 billion next quarter.

nodes.label: Alphabet
nodes.relation: Buys NVIDIA GPUs for Google Cloud while scaling its own TPUs
nodes.summary: Alphabet says 2027 capex will rise significantly, but it is also selling more of its own TPU systems to outside customers.
brief: Both a top GPU buyer and the most credible custom-chip alternative to NVIDIA.
nodes.health: Google Cloud revenue grew 103% to $30.7 billion in the third quarter.

nodes.label: Amazon
nodes.relation: Buys NVIDIA GB300 systems for AWS and builds Trainium chips
nodes.summary: AWS is capacity constrained and Amazon will spend more in 2027, but Trainium is gaining multi-gigawatt commitments.
brief: Its 2027 budget and Trainium push decide how much AWS spend reaches NVIDIA.
nodes.health: AWS grew 39% with a $578 billion backlog; trailing free cash flow is negative $42.4 billion.

nodes.label: Meta
nodes.relation: Buys NVIDIA GB and VR racks for its AI training and ad models
nodes.summary: Meta narrowed 2026 capex to $135-145 billion and has not yet put a number on 2027.
brief: The one big buyer that has not committed to a 2027 capex figure yet.
nodes.health: Revenue grew 26% to $64.6 billion, but free cash flow was negative last quarter.

nodes.label: TrendForce
nodes.relation: Tracks AI server shipments and cloud capex across the supply chain
nodes.summary: TrendForce raised its 2026 AI server growth forecast to nearly 31% and expects top cloud capex near $1.3 trillion in 2027.
brief: Its forecasts show whether server builds and custom chips are moving for or against NVIDIA.
nodes.health: Latest forecast sees top nine cloud capex up nearly 50% in 2027.

nodes.label: IDC
nodes.relation: Tracks server vendor revenue, GPU server units and AI infrastructure spending
nodes.summary: IDC shows GPU server revenue rising on price while custom-accelerator servers grow far faster from a smaller base.
brief: Splits GPU servers from custom-chip servers, the cleanest read on share shift.
nodes.health: Raised its 2026 AI infrastructure forecast to $521 billion from $497 billion.

nodes.label: Dell'Oro Group
nodes.relation: Tracks global data center capex and accelerator spending each quarter
nodes.summary: Dell'Oro counts data center capex up 92% in the second quarter, though part of that is memory price inflation.
brief: Shows how much of total data center spending is landing on accelerators.
nodes.health: Sees data center capex passing $3 trillion by 2030, nearly double January's view.

nodes.label: Silicon Data
nodes.relation: Publishes the daily H100 rental price index that CME compute futures settle against
nodes.summary: Silicon Data's H100 neocloud rental index has climbed from $2.00 last December to about $3.08 an hour.
brief: Rising rent on three-year-old H100s says compute is still scarce, which supports pricing.
nodes.health: H100 index at $3.08 per GPU-hour on November 25, 2026.

nodes.label: OpenRouter
nodes.relation: Routes AI model requests across providers, a live gauge of inference usage
nodes.summary: OpenRouter's token volume has passed a 10 quadrillion annual run rate, driven mostly by AI agents.
brief: Token growth here is an early read on inference demand that ends up on GPUs.
nodes.health: Run rate above 10 quadrillion tokens a year, up from 1.5 quadrillion in May.

signals.headline: TrendForce sees Meta and AWS shifting more AI server volume to their own ASICs in 2027
signals.whyItMatters: If Meta and AWS move more of their 2027 builds to in-house chips, a bigger capex pie does not mean a proportionally bigger NVIDIA slice.
signals.evidence: significantly accelerating deployment of its proprietary AI ASICs in 2027

signals.headline: Worldwide Server Market Revenue Hits Record $166.3 Billion in the Second Quarter of 2026
signals.whyItMatters: Custom-accelerator servers grew more than eight times as fast as GPU servers and GPU units fell, so NVIDIA's growth is leaning on price while rivals gain volume.
signals.evidence: GPU-accelerated servers generated $87.4 billion (+28.1% YoY); other accelerated servers +237.6% to $27.5 billion; GPU unit shipments fell 10.8%

signals.headline: AI Infrastructure Spending Jumps to $121 Billion in Q2 2026; 2026 Forecast Raised to $521 Billion
signals.whyItMatters: IDC raised its 2026 forecast by $24 billion and expects high pricing to last into late 2027, which supports NVIDIA holding firm on price.
signals.evidence: elevated pricing to persist through at least the second half of 2027

signals.headline: Dell'Oro: Data Center capex grew 92% in 2Q-2026 (caveats galore)
signals.whyItMatters: Spending is still concentrated in NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra, but some of the 92% is memory and storage inflation rather than more racks, so headline capex overstates unit demand.
signals.evidence: supply constraints could limit the pace at which planned infrastructure is deployed

signals.headline: Silicon Data H100 rental index reads $3.08 per GPU-hour, up from $2.89 on October 27
signals.whyItMatters: When rent on older H100s keeps rising, buyers are short of compute, which keeps NVIDIA's newer systems priced firmly.

signals.headline: Microsoft's cloud growth accelerates, and so too does the spending
signals.whyItMatters: Microsoft spent $45.2 billion last quarter, guides above $50 billion next, and still cannot meet demand, so its NVIDIA orders are set by capacity, not appetite.
signals.evidence: We still have demand that exceeds supply

signals.headline: Google misses Wall Street expectations, Alphabet stock sinks in early after-hours trading
signals.whyItMatters: Alphabet committed to a big 2027 capex step-up even on a day its stock fell more than 10%, which counts toward the thesis that budgets keep rising.

signals.headline: Alphabet reports Q3 2026 revenue of $127.6 billion
signals.whyItMatters: Pichai says outside customers want TPU systems, so Google is becoming a seller of NVIDIA alternatives, not just a buyer of NVIDIA chips.
signals.evidence: We're also seeing strong demand for our TPU systems across a wide range of customers.

signals.headline: AWS grows 39% and Amazon will spend even more on AI in 2027
signals.whyItMatters: Amazon is holding $220 billion of 2026 capex and says 2027 will be meaningfully higher, a second of the four big budgets still rising.
signals.evidence: Amazon expects to spend "meaningfully more" in 2027

signals.headline: Amazon plans to sell Trainium chips outside AWS from late 2027
signals.whyItMatters: Selling Trainium to third parties would put a second hyperscaler chip in direct competition for NVIDIA's non-hyperscale customers.
signals.evidence: Late in 2027, Amazon also plans to start selling its Trainium AI chips outside AWS

signals.headline: Meta Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results
signals.whyItMatters: Meta narrowed 2026 capex to $135-145 billion but gave no 2027 number, so it is the one big budget the long cannot yet count on.
signals.evidence: still developing our budget and capacity plans for next year

signals.headline: OpenRouter crosses a 10 quadrillion annual token run rate
signals.whyItMatters: Inference usage grew more than sixfold since May, and that usage is what makes the cloud buyers' GPU spending pay back.
signals.evidence: has hit an annualized run rate of over 10 quadrillion tokens

signals.headline: NVIDIA Posts $115.8 Billion Revenue as AI Cloud, Industrial and Enterprise Customers Drive 56% of Data Center Growth
signals.whyItMatters: Non-hyperscale buyers grew 195% to $47.5 billion, so data center growth is no longer resting only on the four big clouds.
signals.evidence: AI cloud, industrial and enterprise: $16.1B to $47.5B, up 195%; hyperscale up 71% to $60.1B

signals.headline: NVIDIA takes on up to $32 billion of conditional obligations tied to AI cloud providers
signals.whyItMatters: Part of the fastest-growing demand is being supported by NVIDIA's own commitments and guarantees, so some orders depend on NVIDIA's balance sheet rather than end-customer budgets.
signals.evidence: up to $32B in conditional obligations tied to AI cloud providers; guarantees up to $118B
